eligibility.title: Who can apply
eligibility.intro: MAPA is for CRMC patients who cannot pay their hospital bill. You do not need to be good with computers — the form is short, and staff can sit with you and help.
eligibility.q1: You are admitted at, or were treated in, CRMC.
eligibility.q2: You have an unpaid hospital bill or billing statement.
eligibility.q3: A CRMC social worker has classified you as an indigent patient.
eligibility.q4: You are the patient, or an immediate family member filing for them.
eligibility.codeHeading: You will need a Patient Access Code
eligibility.codeBody: This is printed and handed to you in person at the CRMC Medical Social Services office. It is never sent by text, email, or social media — and no one online can give you one.

faq.heading: Questions people ask us
faq.intro: If your question isn't here, call or visit us — we would rather explain it than have you guess.
faq.q1: Do I need to pay anything?
faq.a1: No. Applying through MAPA is free, from registration to the release of your Guarantee Letter. CRMC staff and MAPA will never ask for a fee, a deposit, or a 'processing charge'. If anyone asks you for money in exchange for approval, report it to the Medical Social Services office right away.
faq.q2: What is a Patient Access Code and how do I get one?
faq.a2: It is a printed code given to you in person at the CRMC Medical Social Services office, after a social worker confirms you are a CRMC patient with an unpaid hospital bill. The code links your online application to your real hospital record, so it cannot be requested by phone, text, or email. Bring a valid ID and your billing statement.
faq.q3: Can I apply for a family member?
faq.a3: Yes. A spouse, parent, adult child, or authorized representative may file on behalf of the patient — common when the patient is still confined or cannot use a phone. You'll be asked for your relationship to the patient, your own valid ID, and an authorization letter signed by the patient or immediate family.
faq.a4: It depends on how complete your documents are and on each agency's review and available slots. CRMC works to verify documents and schedule your assessment interview as quickly as possible, and you can track every step in your account.
faq.q5: What if I can't come in person for the interview?
faq.a5: Tell your assigned social worker and an online interview via Google Meet can be arranged instead. A link is sent to your registered email and mobile number, and the interview takes about 15–20 minutes. If your signal is weak, it may be done by phone call.
faq.a6: Yes. MAPA is operated by CRMC and handles your data under the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173). Your documents and selfie are used only to verify your identity and your need for assistance, and are shared only with the funding agency your request is endorsed to. You may ask for a copy of your data or ask that it be corrected at any time.

help.title: Help & Support
help.intro: Frequently asked questions about the MAPA {{portal}}.

patientFaqs.q: How do I request medical assistance?
patientFaqs.a: Open Request Assistance, choose the type of help you need (e.g. Hospital Bill), enter the amount, and upload the document required for that type. CRMC reviews it and endorses it to the agencies that can help. You then review your coverage plan, tap Proceed, and complete each agency's requirements.

patientFaqs.q: Where do I get a Patient Access Code?
patientFaqs.a: Patient Access Codes are issued in person by CRMC Medical Social Services. Bring a valid ID. The code follows the format CRMC-YYYY-NNNNN.

A Guarantee Letter (GL) is the official document an agency issues when it approves its share of your bill. Present it at the provider to claim the assistance. GLs are valid for 30 days from issue. A request may receive more than one GL when several agencies co-fund it.

patientFaqs.q: How will I know the status of my request?
patientFaqs.a: You'll receive in-app + email notifications at each step — when CRMC endorses your request, when agencies review it, and at each approval. The Request Assistance page shows your coverage plan and how much has been secured toward zero balance.

patientFaqs.q: How do I join my online interview?
patientFaqs.a: If an agency schedules an interview, a Google Meet link appears on your Interviews page and Dashboard. Click it a few minutes before your slot — no install needed on a recent browser.

patientFaqs.q: Do I choose which agencies help me?
patientFaqs.a: No — you submit one request and CRMC routes it to the agencies that can cover it, sometimes splitting it across several to reach a zero balance. You can have one active request at a time.

patientFaqs.q: How do I withdraw my request?
patientFaqs.a: You can withdraw a request while it's still being reviewed by CRMC (before it's endorsed). After it's endorsed to agencies, contact CRMC or the agency through Messages.

whatIsMapa.title: What is MAPA?
whatIsMapa.content: MAPA (Medical Assistance Portal Access) is the official online system of Cotabato Regional Medical Center (CRMC) for processing medical assistance applications. It allows patients to apply for financial or material assistance from partner government agencies such as DSWD, PCSO, and the Malasakit Center — all in one place, without lining up at multiple offices.

whoCanUse.title: Who can use MAPA?
whoCanUse.content: Any patient of CRMC who has been assessed by Medical Social Services can register and use MAPA. You will receive a Patient Access Code (format: CRMC-YYYY-XXXXX) from the CRMC Medical Social Services office. You must have this code to create an account.

register.title: How do I register?
register.s1: Visit CRMC Medical Social Services to be assessed and receive your Patient Access Code.
register.s2: Go to the MAPA registration page and fill in your full name, email, contact number, and address.
register.s3: Enter your Patient Access Code and click Verify to confirm it.
register.s4: Create a secure password and submit the form.
register.s5: Your account is created. Log in with your email and password.

upload.title: What documents do I submit?
upload.s1: Open Request Assistance — the required documents are listed there as a checklist.
upload.s2: Attach a clear photo or scan of each one (e.g., Valid ID, Billing Statement, Medical Certificate, Barangay Indigency).
upload.s3: For your Valid ID, the app does a quick on-device name check to help confirm it's yours — it never blocks you.
upload.s4: Take a live selfie when prompted; CRMC compares it to your ID to confirm your identity.
upload.s5: Submit. CRMC reviews and verifies your documents before endorsing your request to agencies.
upload.s6: If CRMC marks a document for correction, you'll be notified — re-upload it from your request.
upload.note: Tip: A Valid ID, once verified, carries over to your future requests. Your Billing Statement (Statement of Account) is needed fresh for each request.

apply.title: How do I request assistance?
apply.s1: Go to Request Assistance from the sidebar or the bottom tab.
apply.s2: Choose the type of assistance you need and enter the amount you need help with, based on your billing statement.
apply.s3: Attach your billing statement (Statement of Account), confirm the declaration, and submit your request.
apply.s4: CRMC reviews your request and endorses it to one or more agencies that can help cover your bill.
apply.s5: Open Request Assistance to see your coverage plan, then tap Proceed to send it to those agencies.
apply.s6: Complete each agency's requirements and join any scheduled online interview.
apply.s7: Once an agency approves, you will receive a Guarantee Letter to claim your assistance.
apply.note: Important: You can have only one active request at a time. Track its progress anytime under My Application.

withdraw.title: Can I cancel or withdraw my application?
withdraw.s1: Go to My Application from the sidebar.
withdraw.s2: Find your active application under the In Progress tab.
withdraw.s3: Scroll to the bottom of the application card.
withdraw.s4: Tap Withdraw Application — a confirmation will appear.
withdraw.s5: Tap Yes, Withdraw to confirm. The spot will be returned and you can apply again.
withdraw.note: You can only withdraw while your application is in Pending Review status. Once the agency starts reviewing, withdrawal is no longer available.

cofunding.title: What is co-funding? Why do I see multiple agencies?
cofunding.content: MAPA uses a co-funding model. You file ONE request stating your bill and the amount you need. CRMC verifies your documents and interviews you, then endorses your request to one or more partner agencies (DSWD, PCSO, Malasakit, AMBaG) that together cover your bill toward zero balance. Each agency makes its own funding decision and issues its own Guarantee Letter for the portion it covers. You never have to apply to each agency separately — CRMC routes the case for you.
cofunding.note: After CRMC endorses your request, you'll see a Coverage Plan listing each agency. Tap Proceed to confirm and start their reviews.

intakeWizard.title: What is the Household Intake Wizard?
intakeWizard.content: After CRMC starts reviewing your documents, you'll be asked to fill a 5-step household form covering your family, income, expenses, and medical situation. This is the factual part of the Unified Intake Sheet — CRMC adds the assessment portion during your interview. Your social worker uses this to recommend which agencies should fund your request.
intakeWizard.s1: Open Request Assistance and tap the Household Intake link, or go directly to /patient/request/<id>/intake.
intakeWizard.s2: Step 1 — Household: list each family member living with you.
intakeWizard.s3: Step 2-3 — Income and expenses: monthly income, employment, and household expenses.
intakeWizard.s4: Step 4 — Medical: diagnosis, attending physician, hospital case number, estimated cost.
intakeWizard.s5: Step 5 — Review: confirm everything and submit. Auto-save runs every 2 seconds so you won't lose work.
intakeWizard.note: You can save partial progress and return any time before submission. The wizard remembers where you left off.

requestLifecycle.title: What are the stages of my request?
requestLifecycle.content: Your request goes through six stages from submission to fully funded. The progress stepper on My Application shows where you are.
requestLifecycle.submittedDesc: You filed the request. CRMC will start reviewing your attached documents shortly.
requestLifecycle.underReviewDesc: CRMC is verifying your documents. You may be asked to re-upload any unclear or rejected ones.
requestLifecycle.assessmentDesc: CRMC has scheduled your single assessment interview via Google Meet. After the interview, your social worker completes the Unified Intake Sheet.
requestLifecycle.endorsedDesc: CRMC has routed your request to one or more agencies. Review the Coverage Plan on My Application and tap Proceed to start their reviews.
requestLifecycle.partiallyFundedDesc: At least one agency has approved their portion. Others may still be reviewing — your bill is being progressively covered.
requestLifecycle.fullyFundedDesc: Every approving agency has covered their portion and your bill is at (or near) zero balance. Download each agency's Guarantee Letter and present it at the named provider.

statuses.title: What do the per-agency (slice) statuses mean?
statuses.content: Each agency CRMC endorses your request to gets its own card on My Application. Each card has its own status as the agency processes your portion.
statuses.endorsedDesc: CRMC has routed your request to this agency. The agency hasn't started reviewing yet — you need to tap Proceed on the Coverage Plan first.
statuses.reviewingDesc: You tapped Proceed and the agency is now reviewing whether to fund this portion of your bill.
statuses.awaitingInfoDesc: The agency needs something from you (a clearer document, a missed detail, etc.). You'll see their message and a re-upload prompt.
statuses.approvedDesc: The agency approved a specific amount toward your bill. Their Guarantee Letter is being prepared.
statuses.certDesc: The agency has issued and signed their Guarantee Letter. Download it from My Application and present it at the named provider (e.g., CRMC Billing, Mercury Drug).
statuses.rejectedDesc: This agency couldn't cover its portion. CRMC may re-endorse to another agency, or your overall request may stay partially funded.

interview.title: How do I join my interview?
interview.s1: Go to Interviews from the sidebar to see your scheduled interviews.
interview.s2: Note the date, time, and Google Meet link for your interview.
interview.s3: At the scheduled time, click the Join Meet button to enter the video call.
interview.s4: Prepare your original documents in case the agency asks to see them on camera.
interview.s5: After the interview, the agency will update your application status.
interview.note: If you need to reschedule, contact the agency directly through the Messages feature.

download.title: How do I download my Guarantee Letter?
download.s1: Go to My Application from the sidebar.
download.s2: Find your approved application — it shows a green panel with the approved amount, purpose, and the provider it is payable to.
download.s3: Wait until the agency uploads the wet-signed copy. You will receive an in-portal notification when it is ready.
download.s4: Click the thumbnail to view the signed Guarantee Letter, or click Download to save a copy to your device.
download.s5: Present the signed Guarantee Letter (printed or shown on your phone) at the provider named on it (hospital billing, pharmacy, etc.).
download.note: The Guarantee Letter is valid for 30 days from the date of issuance. The named provider may bill the agency directly for the guaranteed amount — you are not responsible for the guaranteed portion.

contact.title: How do I contact the admin or agency?
contact.content: Go to Messages from the sidebar to view all your conversations. Tap the New Message button at the top right to start a new conversation with hospital staff or your assigned agency. You can message them directly if you have questions about your application, documents, or need to reschedule an interview.

forgotPw.title: I forgot my password. What do I do?
forgotPw.content: On the Login page, click "Forgot Password?" and enter your registered email address. A password reset link will be sent to your email. Click the link to set a new password. If you did not receive the email, check your spam or junk folder. For further help, contact CRMC Medical Social Services.
